definitions.explanation: The time at seven hours past midnight or noon.

examples.japanese: {七時|しちじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。
examples.english: I wake up at seven o'clock.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{七時|しちじ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧です。
examples.english: The meeting starts at seven o'clock.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧{七時|しちじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: I leave home at seven o'clock every morning.

notes:
PRONUNCIATION:
Both しちじ and ななじ are used. しちじ is the standard reading; ななじ is often used to keep しちじ apart from いちじ (⟦{一時|いちじ}→一時：01799_ichiji⟧, one o'clock), for example in announcements and on the phone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧{七時|しちじ}: 7 a.m.
- ⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧{七時|しちじ}: 7 p.m.
- {七時半|しちじはん}: 7:30
- {七時|しちじ}⟦ちょうど→ちょうど：02916_choudo⟧: exactly 7 o'clock
- {七時|しちじ}{過|す}ぎ: past 7 o'clock

WATCH OUT:
7 is read しち or なな depending on the word: ⟦{七月|しちがつ}→七月：00667_shichigatsu⟧ (July) but ⟦{七|なな}つ→七つ：02926_nanatsu⟧ (seven things), and ⟦{七日|なのか}→七日：02927_nanoka⟧ (the 7th day) has a reading of its own.
